The **UCL Slade School of Fine Art** (informally **The Slade**) is the [art school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_school "Art school") of [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London") (UCL) and is based in London, England. It has been ranked as the UK's top art and design educational institution.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-4) The school is organised as a department of UCL's [Faculty of Arts and Humanities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCL_Faculty_of_Arts_and_Humanities "UCL Faculty of Arts and Humanities").
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slade_School_of_Fine_Art&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9b/SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg/250px-SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SLADE_1905_B_sampled.jpeg)Students at the Slade in 1905
The school was founded in University College on 2 October 1871 following an endowment from the will of the lawyer and philanthropist [Felix Slade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Slade "Felix Slade") (1788–1868) who bequeathed £35,000 to establish three Chairs in [Fine Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fine_Art "Fine Art"), to be based at Oxford University, Cambridge University and [University College London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_College_London "University College London"). An additional six scholarships of £50 per annum were endowed to University College. The college itself provided £5000 to build the Slade School as part of the college quadrangle in Gower Street, premises which the School still occupies today.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-5)
Distinguished past teachers include [Henry Tonks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Tonks "Henry Tonks"), [Wilson Steer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Steer "Wilson Steer"), [Randolph Schwabe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randolph_Schwabe "Randolph Schwabe"), [William Coldstream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coldstream "William Coldstream"), [Andrew Forge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Forge "Andrew Forge"), [Lucian Freud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucian_Freud "Lucian Freud"), [John Hilliard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hilliard_\(artist\) "John Hilliard \(artist\)"), [Bruce McLean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_McLean "Bruce McLean"), [Alfred Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Gerrard "Alfred Gerrard") and [Phyllida Barlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phyllida_Barlow "Phyllida Barlow"). [Edward Allington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Allington "Edward Allington") was Professor of Fine Art and Head of Graduate Sculpture until his death in 2017.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-icl-7)
Two of its most important periods were immediately before, and immediately after, the turn of the twentieth century, described by Henry Tonks as its two 'crises of brilliance'. The first included the students [Augustus John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus_John "Augustus John"), [William Orpen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Orpen "William Orpen") and [Percy Wyndham Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percy_Wyndham_Lewis "Percy Wyndham Lewis"); the second – which has been chronicled in [David Boyd Haycock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Boyd_Haycock "David Boyd Haycock")'s _A Crisis of Brilliance: Five Young British Artists and the Great War_ – included the students [Dora Carrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dora_Carrington "Dora Carrington"), [Mark Gertler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Gertler_\(artist\) "Mark Gertler \(artist\)"), [Paul Nash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Nash_\(artist\) "Paul Nash \(artist\)"), [C.R.W. Nevinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.R.W._Nevinson "C.R.W. Nevinson") and [Stanley Spencer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Spencer "Stanley Spencer").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-8)
Another notable period followed the Second World War, under the directorship of [William Coldstream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Coldstream "William Coldstream"), who brought in [Lucian Freud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucian_Freud "Lucian Freud") to teach, and whose students included [Paula Rego](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paula_Rego "Paula Rego"), [Michael Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Andrews_\(artist\) "Michael Andrews \(artist\)") and the filmmaker [Lorenza Mazzetti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenza_Mazzetti "Lorenza Mazzetti"). Coldstream was responsible for the creation of the [Slade Film Department](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/slade/sladearchive/history-of-the-slade-film-project/), the first in any British university, in 1960, with [Thorold Dickinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorold_Dickinson "Thorold Dickinson") as chief lecturer. Filmmakers associated with the Slade Film Department include [Derek Jarman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Jarman "Derek Jarman") and [Peter Whitehead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Whitehead_\(filmmaker\) "Peter Whitehead \(filmmaker\)").
## Slade Centre for Electronic Media in Fine Art
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slade_School_of_Fine_Art&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Slade Centre for Electronic Media in Fine Art")]
The Slade Centre for Electronic Media in Fine Art (SCEMFA) was opened in 1995. The centre provides opportunities for research into [electronic media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_media "Electronic media") and fine art with the goal of contributing to debate on national and international levels. The Slade had previously been home to Malcolm Hughes's Computer and Experimental Department in the 1970s.
In 1997 SCEMFA presented _Collision_ , a public lecture series by artists, writers, and curators working with [interactivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interactivity "Interactivity"), [telematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telematics "Telematics"), and digital works. This exhibition was followed by _Spontaneous Reaction_ , a week-long seminar funded by the [Arts Council of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arts_Council_of_England "Arts Council of England"), which took a critical look at interactivity with participants from a variety of disciplines, including psychology, architecture, and [computer science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_science "Computer science").
Throughout 1998, SCEMFA collaborated with Channel 4 UK to organise _Cached_ , a monthly event held at the [Institute of Contemporary Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_of_Contemporary_Arts "Institute of Contemporary Arts"), London. Funded by the Arts Council, this series investigated the conceptual and practical issues of producing art for the internet through a series of artists presentations.
## Art collection
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slade_School_of_Fine_Art&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Art collection")]
The Slade art collection was started when the yearly prizes awarded to top students was combined with a collection scheme in 1897 and the Summer Composition Prize and the Figure and Head Painting Prizes began to be kept by the school.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-YP-9) Works by students and staff of the Slade School of Fine Art form the basis of the UCL Art museum today.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slade_School_of_Fine_Art#cite_note-YP-9)

## Teaching
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Slade_School_of_Fine_Art&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Teaching")]
The faculty currently offers the following programs:
Undergraduate studies
  * 3-year BFA in Fine Art
  * 4-year BA in Fine Art


Graduate studies
  * 2-academic year (18 months) MFA in Fine Art
  * 2-calendar (24 months) MA in Fine Art
  * 1-term, 2-term, of 1-year Graduate Affiliate Study


Research
  * MPhil or PhD in Fine Art
